pull_request.title: Preserve EPnP beta magnitudes when sign estimates are zero
pull_request.body:
## Problem

EPnP uses signs of least-squares coefficients to choose the directions of independently estimated beta magnitudes. A coefficient of `0.0` or `-0.0` currently contributes a zero multiplier and can erase a nonzero magnitude.

For example, the observed first 6-by-3 QR result `[-0.0, 4.575284e-05, 179.5135956]` produces an entirely zero two-vector candidate. Its scale becomes non-finite, and the batched pose SVD fails before another candidate can be selected.

## Change

Use +1 for a zero direction estimate in the two-, three- and four-vector initializations. Nonzero signs and magnitude calculations keep their existing behavior.

Fixes #546.

This selects a deterministic direction when an orientation coefficient is zero; it does not claim a unique optimal orientation from the remaining quadratic estimates. Truly all-zero estimates remain degenerate, and the existing `sqrt(abs(S))` derivative at a zero magnitude is not changed.

## Validation

The [exact-source two-version run](https://github.com/Afloat16/pypose/actions/runs/44040766108) validates production commit `3706c43d4a345baf8206499465801c4ac7051a71` on CPU Torch **2.5.1 and 2.6.0**.

On each version:

- The 88 new tests give **76 failures and 12 passing controls on unchanged main**, then all pass with this patch. They cover positive/negative zero, all sign-bearing positions, float32/float64, multiple batch axes, nonzero direction controls, all-zero estimates, and complete camera-pose regressions.
- The full repository suite gives **488 passed, 18 skipped**.
- 64 independent nonzero-coefficient comparisons preserve all four candidate outputs and their coefficient gradients bit for bit.
- Eight ordinary public calls preserve poses bit for bit and match point/pixel/intrinsics gradients.
- Eight public camera calls replay a zero first coefficient: all eight original calls fail at the non-finite SVD candidate; all eight patched calls recover the known camera pose.

The public replay tests explicitly inject the previously observed zero coefficient and use the existing `gelsd` beta solver to keep the rest of the comparison deterministic. They are not a natural failure-frequency measurement, and production solver selection is unchanged.

Magnitude regressions for the four-vector initialization compare the set of squared magnitudes independently of its existing coefficient ordering. The nonzero compatibility checks separately preserve current outputs.

The history audit includes all 82 distinct PnP sources across 135 commits reachable from 343 fetched upstream PR heads and 69 existing account branches, including the earlier NumPy implementations and renamed helpers. The zeroing sign convention is present throughout; no equivalent zero-direction handling was found.

limits: Camera regression explicitly injects the observed first coefficient zero and configures existing gelsd for reproducibility; no natural-frequency claim.
True all-zero estimates remain degenerate. No finite-gradient promise at sqrt(abs(S)) zero boundary.
Legacy NumPy already reconstructs full-four coefficient order correctly; restoring that ordering is excluded as previously implemented, not counted or included in this patch.
The first independent 44-case review established zero-sign magnitude retention using historical slot mapping; corrected review explicitly does not certify full-four mathematical ordering.
